title: Introduce Cost Lens: tenant-aware quantization profiler and batch/cache defaults
author: Ava Martinez
description: Context: Customers frequently ask for one-click recommendations for batching, cache retention, and quantization profiles per tenant. Existing autotuners produce candidate profiles but lack a unified, explainable view that ties unit economics (tokens/op), latency SLO curves, and quantization-induced quality delta. This PR introduces 'Cost Lens' — a deterministic profiler and simulator that: 1) consumes replayed/recent traffic samples and telemetry to synthesize tenant-specific batch/cache default suggestions, 2) evaluates candidate quantization profiles (fp16/int8/4-bit QAT-sim proxies) against a small eval set and produces a quality vs. cost scatter, and 3) emits artifacts consumable by Console and the CLI for safe rollout. Summary of changes: - New service module cost_lens that performs sampling, deterministic simulation, and scoring. - Telemetry schema additions (cost_lens.v1) for the Cost Lens outputs and the new 'sample_weight' field used for tenant-weighted aggregation. - A lightweight CLI command (rw cost-lens profile --tenant) to preview and export profiles as YAML. - Console integration hooks: final JSON artifact is written to /artifacts/cost-lens/<tenant> for the console uploader. - Safety: rollout annotations include a conservative fallback policy that prefers higher-precision models when latency regressions exceed thresholds. Motivation: Reduce time-to-first-good-profile for Dedicated/Private customers and give platform teams a transparent artifact to reason about tradeoffs. Checklist: - [x] deterministic sampler implemented and unit-tested - [x] quant-sim proxies and simple eval harness added - [x] telemetry schema and migration added - [x] CLI preview/export implemented - [x] Console artifact writer and unit tests - [x] end-to-end perf smoke test included - [x] docs describing acceptance criteria and suggested canary steps Implementation notes: The profiler runs off sampled traces collected by the existing prefiller replay pipeline; sampling preserves sequence-length and prompt-type distributions. Simulation is deterministic: we re-run requests through the serving runtime in a dry-run mode (no external network calls) where the kernel selection is emulated and latency numbers come from measured microbenchmarks stored in the kernel-catalog cache. Quantization quality is approximated by the quant-sim proxy which applies per-layer noise profiles derived from small in-memory calibration runs; we explicitly avoid full QAT during profiling to keep runtime cheap. Output: For each tenant the Cost Lens produces a JSON artifact that contains: recommended_batch_shape, cache_retention_ms, ranked_quant_profiles (with estimated cost_delta, latency_delta, and expected quality_delta), and a 'cost_lens_report' which is a flattened cost vs latency curve. Rollout safety: every profile includes a safe_fallback field and a confidence score. When confidence < 0.6, the CLI defaults to --dry-run. Security & privacy: sampling runs inside the private telemetry pipeline; artifacts omit raw prompt text and only keep hashed prompt signatures used for eval set matching. Related work and follow-ups: this PR adds the profiling engine and integration points; follow-ups planned: 1) UI for interactive profile tuning in Console (ENG-1330), 2) tenant-level automated rollouts in Dedicated (ENG-1331), 3) longer-running background auto-recalibration (ENG-1332).

feat(telemetry): add cost_lens.v1 schema and migration
feat(cli): rw cost-lens profile preview/export command
chore(tests): add end-to-end perf smoke test and unit tests
docs: add cost lens design doc and rollout guidance
review_comments: Rohit Kapoor: Nice work overall. Please add a brief note in the docs about the calibration dataset size and how it can bias the quality_delta. Also the deterministic dry-run mode needs an opt-out flag for local dev runs.
Ava Martinez: Added a section in docs/README.md about calibration sizes and default (50 samples per prompt-signature). Implemented --allow-local-dryrun on the CLI to make this explicit.
Lina Zhao: Tests look good but e2e smoke is flaky on GHA matrix - seeing a 2s tail occasionally. Can we pin the microbenchmark values for CI?
Ava Martinez: Pinned the kernel-catalog snapshot used in CI and added retry logic around the e2e harness. Re-ran CI and the flake didn't reproduce.
Ethan Cole: Telemetry migration looks fine. Question: should we include tenant-privacy level in the artifact? If a customer has 'no-derived-profiles' we must not emit artifacts.
Ava Martinez: Respecting tenant flags is now implemented in telemetry migration. The profiler early-exits if tenant policy forbids derived profiles. Added a unit test for that.
Rohit Kapoor: Approve after addressing the minor doc wording.
release_notes: Added Cost Lens: tenant-aware profiler that suggests batching, cache retention, and ranked quant profiles with safety fallbacks. Accessible via 'rw cost-lens profile' CLI and produces artifacts consumable by Console. Not enabled by default for tenants that opt out of derived artifacts.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps quant-sim as an approximation to prevent long profiling runs; if teams need QAT-grade validation they should run the Canary workflow described in rollout-playbook.md. The artifact shape is stable for 1.0 but the confidence scoring may be tuned in follow-ups.
